IPO Readiness Assessment.shortDescription: Comprehensive assessment of company structure, financials, and governance before commencing the IPO process.
IPO Readiness Assessment.longDescription: We evaluate your company's readiness across governance, financials, and compliance against IPO eligibility norms, identifying gaps to address before filing.
benefits: Clear roadmap before committing to IPO costs
Identifies gaps early to avoid delays
Improved confidence for the listing process

process.title: Report Delivery
process.description: Present readiness report and action plan.

faqs.question: How early should readiness assessment start?
faqs.answer: Ideally 12-18 months before the intended IPO.

faqs.question: What are common readiness gaps?
faqs.answer: Board composition, related-party transactions, and financial reporting standards.

faqs.question: Does this replace due diligence?
faqs.answer: No, it's a preliminary assessment; formal due diligence follows separately.

IPO Legal Due Diligence.shortDescription: Detailed legal review of corporate records, contracts, and liabilities before IPO.
IPO Legal Due Diligence.longDescription: We conduct comprehensive legal due diligence covering corporate records, material contracts, litigation, and regulatory compliance ahead of your IPO filing.
benefits: Identifies legal risks before public disclosure

process.title: Scope Definition
process.description: Define diligence scope and materiality thresholds.

faqs.question: Who uses the due diligence report?
faqs.answer: Merchant bankers, legal counsel, and the board for prospectus preparation.

faqs.question: How long does legal due diligence take?
faqs.answer: Typically 4-6 weeks depending on company complexity.

faqs.question: What risks are commonly flagged?
faqs.answer: Title defects, pending litigation, and non-compliant contracts.

IPO Corporate Restructuring.shortDescription: Assistance in restructuring shareholding and corporate arrangements to meet IPO eligibility.
IPO Corporate Restructuring.longDescription: We help simplify group structures, consolidate shareholding, and address corporate arrangements that could hinder IPO eligibility or investor comfort.

process.title: Structure Review
process.description: Map current group and shareholding structure.

process.title: Restructuring Plan
process.description: Design simplified structure aligned with IPO norms.

faqs.question: Why is corporate restructuring needed before IPO?
faqs.answer: To present a clean, comprehensible structure to investors and regulators.

faqs.question: Does restructuring affect tax position?
faqs.answer: It can; tax implications should be assessed alongside restructuring.

faqs.question: How long before IPO should this start?
faqs.answer: At least 12 months in advance for complex structures.

IPO Regulatory Compliance.shortDescription: Ensure compliance with SEBI and stock exchange regulations throughout the IPO process.
IPO Regulatory Compliance.longDescription: We guide you through the full spectrum of regulatory requirements under SEBI ICDR regulations and exchange listing norms for a compliant IPO journey.

faqs.question: What is SEBI ICDR?
faqs.answer: The Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements regulations governing IPOs.

faqs.question: Who reviews the IPO documents?
faqs.answer: SEBI and the stock exchanges review the draft offer document before approval.

faqs.question: What happens if SEBI raises observations?
faqs.answer: The company must address them before proceeding to the final offer document.

Draft Red Herring Prospectus.shortDescription: Preparation of the Draft Red Herring Prospectus for SEBI filing and public disclosure.
Draft Red Herring Prospectus.longDescription: We assist in compiling the DRHP covering business, financials, risk factors, and offer details in compliance with SEBI disclosure norms.
features: Business and industry section drafting support

process.title: Information Gathering
process.description: Collect business, financial, and risk data.

process.title: Filing
process.description: Finalize and file DRHP with SEBI.

faqs.question: What does DRHP stand for?
faqs.answer: Draft Red Herring Prospectus, the preliminary IPO disclosure document.

faqs.question: Is DRHP publicly available?
faqs.answer: Yes, it is made public upon SEBI filing for stakeholder comments.

faqs.question: How does DRHP differ from RHP?
faqs.answer: DRHP is the draft version; RHP is the updated version filed closer to the offer.

Red Herring Prospectus.shortDescription: Finalize the Red Herring Prospectus incorporating SEBI observations before the public offer.
Red Herring Prospectus.longDescription: We help finalize the RHP by incorporating SEBI's observations and updated financial/business information ahead of the public issue opening.

process.title: Observation Review
process.description: Analyze SEBI's observations on the DRHP.

process.title: Filing
process.description: File the RHP with RoC and exchanges.

faqs.question: What triggers RHP preparation?
faqs.answer: Receipt of SEBI's final observations on the DRHP.

faqs.question: Is pricing included in RHP?
faqs.answer: A price band is typically disclosed, with final price fixed later.

faqs.question: Where is RHP filed?
faqs.answer: With the Registrar of Companies and stock exchanges.

IPO Prospectus Preparation.shortDescription: Prepare the final prospectus incorporating issue price and allotment details post-IPO.
IPO Prospectus Preparation.longDescription: We assist in preparing the final prospectus with the determined issue price, allotment basis, and other conclusive details required after the offer closes.
features: Final pricing and allotment detail compilation
benefits: Compliant closure of the IPO process

process.title: Data Finalization
process.description: Confirm final price and allotment details.

faqs.question: When is the final prospectus filed?
faqs.answer: After the issue closes and allotment is finalized.

faqs.question: Does the prospectus differ from RHP?
faqs.answer: Yes, it includes final pricing and allotment information absent in the RHP.

faqs.question: Who receives the final prospectus?
faqs.answer: Filed with RoC and made available to investors and exchanges.

IPO Offer Document Review.shortDescription: Independent review of your IPO offer document for accuracy, completeness, and compliance.
IPO Offer Document Review.longDescription: We provide an independent review of your offer document, checking for factual accuracy, completeness of disclosures, and compliance with SEBI requirements.

faqs.question: Who typically requests this review?
faqs.answer: Boards, audit committees, or independent directors seeking assurance.

faqs.question: Is this a substitute for merchant banker due diligence?
faqs.answer: No, it's a complementary independent check.

faqs.question: What issues are commonly found?
faqs.answer: Inconsistent figures, incomplete risk factors, or outdated information.

SEBI Compliance Advisory.shortDescription: Advisory on SEBI regulatory compliance applicable to the IPO and post-listing obligations.
SEBI Compliance Advisory.longDescription: We provide ongoing guidance on SEBI regulations covering disclosure norms, insider trading rules, and other compliance requirements relevant to your listing journey.
requirements: Company structure and listing stage details

process.title: Advisory
process.description: Provide guidance on specific compliance areas.

process.title: Update Monitoring
process.description: Track regulatory changes affecting the company.

faqs.question: What SEBI regulations apply post-listing?
faqs.answer: LODR regulations, insider trading rules, and periodic disclosure norms.

faqs.question: Is this relevant only during IPO?
faqs.answer: No, ongoing compliance is required throughout the company's listed life.

faqs.question: What happens on SEBI non-compliance?
faqs.answer: Penalties, show-cause notices, or other regulatory action may follow.

Stock Exchange Listing Compliance.shortDescription: Ensure compliance with stock exchange listing requirements throughout the IPO process.
Stock Exchange Listing Compliance.longDescription: We manage compliance with exchange-specific listing agreements, eligibility criteria, and documentation requirements for a smooth listing.

faqs.question: Which exchanges can a company list on?
faqs.answer: NSE, BSE, or both, depending on eligibility and choice.

faqs.question: What are common eligibility criteria?
faqs.answer: Minimum net worth, track record, and public shareholding requirements.

faqs.question: Is listing agreement compliance ongoing?
faqs.answer: Yes, it continues throughout the company's listed status.

IPO Due Diligence Certificate.shortDescription: Prepare due diligence certificates required to be filed with SEBI during the IPO process.
IPO Due Diligence Certificate.longDescription: We assist in compiling and issuing the various due diligence certificates mandated under SEBI regulations at different stages of the IPO.

faqs.question: Who issues due diligence certificates?
faqs.answer: Typically the lead merchant banker, supported by legal and financial advisors.

faqs.question: At what stages are these required?
faqs.answer: At DRHP filing, RHP filing, and other key milestones.

faqs.question: What happens if certification is delayed?
faqs.answer: It can delay the overall IPO timeline.

IPO Shareholder Restructuring.shortDescription: Restructure shareholder arrangements to align with IPO eligibility and market expectations.
IPO Shareholder Restructuring.longDescription: We help streamline shareholder agreements, exit existing special rights, and align cap table structures suitable for a public listing.
benefits: Cleaner cap table for public investors

faqs.question: Why terminate shareholder agreements before IPO?
faqs.answer: Special rights are generally incompatible with public shareholding norms.

faqs.question: What happens to preference shares pre-IPO?
faqs.answer: They are typically converted to equity before listing.

faqs.question: Does this affect existing investor rights?
faqs.answer: Yes, most special rights terminate upon listing per standard agreements.

Capital Structure Review.shortDescription: Review and optimize your capital structure ahead of the IPO for investor appeal and compliance.
Capital Structure Review.longDescription: We assess your debt-equity mix, share classes, and capital structure to ensure it aligns with IPO norms and investor expectations.

process.title: Structure Analysis
process.description: Review current debt-equity and share structure.

process.title: Benchmarking
process.description: Compare against peer and market norms.

faqs.question: Why review capital structure before IPO?
faqs.answer: To ensure it's simple, compliant, and appealing to public investors.

faqs.question: Does high debt affect IPO valuation?
faqs.answer: Yes, excessive leverage can affect investor perception and pricing.

faqs.question: Are multiple share classes allowed for listed companies?
faqs.answer: Restricted; most listings require a simplified single-class structure.

Promoter Compliance Review.shortDescription: Review promoter-related disclosures and compliance requirements ahead of the IPO.
Promoter Compliance Review.longDescription: We assess promoter background, related-party dealings, and disclosure obligations to ensure full compliance with SEBI promoter norms.

faqs.question: What is promoter lock-in?
faqs.answer: A restriction preventing promoters from selling shares for a specified period post-IPO.

faqs.question: Are related-party transactions disclosed in the prospectus?
faqs.answer: Yes, material related-party transactions must be disclosed.

faqs.question: What is the minimum promoter contribution requirement?
faqs.answer: Typically 20% of post-issue capital, subject to lock-in.

Corporate Governance Advisory.shortDescription: Advisory on strengthening corporate governance practices to meet listing requirements.
Corporate Governance Advisory.longDescription: We help design board composition, committee structures, and governance policies aligned with SEBI LODR requirements for listed companies.

process.title: Structure Design
process.description: Design compliant board and committee structure.

faqs.question: How many independent directors are required?
faqs.answer: At least one-third to half of the board, depending on chairman status.

faqs.question: What committees are mandatory?
faqs.answer: Audit committee, nomination and remuneration committee, and stakeholder relationship committee.

faqs.question: When must governance structure be in place?
faqs.answer: Before the IPO filing, and continuously maintained post-listing.

IPO Related Party Review.shortDescription: Review and document related-party transactions for accurate IPO disclosure compliance.
IPO Related Party Review.longDescription: We identify, assess, and document all related-party transactions to ensure accurate and complete disclosure in the offer document.

process.title: Identification
process.description: Map all related parties and transactions.

faqs.question: What qualifies as a related party?
faqs.answer: Promoters, key managerial personnel, and entities under common control, among others.

faqs.question: Are all related-party transactions disclosed?
faqs.answer: Material transactions above prescribed thresholds are typically disclosed.

faqs.question: Why does arm's-length pricing matter?
faqs.answer: It demonstrates fairness and reduces governance concerns for investors.

IPO Litigation Review.shortDescription: Review pending litigation and legal proceedings for accurate IPO disclosure and risk assessment.
IPO Litigation Review.longDescription: We compile and assess all pending litigation involving the company, promoters, and directors to ensure accurate disclosure and risk factor drafting.

process.title: Documentation
process.description: Prepare disclosure and risk factor drafts.

faqs.question: Whose litigation must be disclosed?
faqs.answer: The company, its subsidiaries, promoters, and directors.

faqs.question: Is every case disclosed regardless of size?
faqs.answer: No, materiality thresholds determine which cases require disclosure.

faqs.question: How does litigation affect IPO timing?
faqs.answer: Material pending cases may require resolution or careful risk disclosure before proceeding.

IPO Contract Review.shortDescription: Review material contracts and agreements for IPO disclosure and risk assessment.
IPO Contract Review.longDescription: We review material contracts — customer, supplier, financing, and other key agreements — to identify disclosure requirements and potential risks.
requirements: List of key contracts and agreements

faqs.question: What makes a contract 'material'?
faqs.answer: Significant value, strategic importance, or impact on business continuity.

faqs.question: Are all contracts disclosed in the prospectus?
faqs.answer: No, only material contracts meeting disclosure thresholds.

faqs.question: What risks are commonly identified?
faqs.answer: Termination clauses, exclusivity restrictions, and change-of-control provisions.

IPO Intellectual Property Review.shortDescription: Review IP ownership, registrations, and risks relevant to IPO disclosure requirements.
IPO Intellectual Property Review.longDescription: We verify ownership and registration status of trademarks, patents, and other IP assets material to the business, ensuring accurate prospectus disclosure.
benefits: Confirms clean IP ownership for investors

faqs.question: Why review IP for an IPO?
faqs.answer: To confirm the company legally owns and can rely on its key intangible assets.

faqs.question: Are pending IP applications disclosed?
faqs.answer: Yes, material pending applications are typically disclosed.

faqs.question: What if IP ownership is unclear?
faqs.answer: Steps should be taken to formalize ownership before the IPO filing.

IPO Employment Law Review.shortDescription: Review employment contracts, policies, and labour law compliance ahead of the IPO.
IPO Employment Law Review.longDescription: We assess employment agreements, ESOP schemes, and labour law compliance to identify risks and ensure accurate IPO disclosure.

process.title: Compliance Check
process.description: Assess ESOP and labour law compliance.

faqs.question: Is ESOP disclosure mandatory in the prospectus?
faqs.answer: Yes, material ESOP schemes require disclosure.

faqs.question: What labour laws are commonly reviewed?
faqs.answer: PF, ESI, gratuity, and applicable state labour regulations.

faqs.question: Can pending employment disputes affect IPO?
faqs.answer: Material disputes require disclosure and risk assessment.

IPO Tax Due Diligence.shortDescription: Review tax records and potential liabilities to identify risks before the IPO.
IPO Tax Due Diligence.longDescription: We conduct a thorough tax due diligence covering direct and indirect tax compliance, pending litigation, and contingent liabilities relevant to the IPO.
features: Direct and indirect tax compliance review
benefits: Identifies tax risks before public disclosure

process.title: Scope Definition
process.description: Define review period and tax areas.

process.title: Detailed Review
process.description: Examine tax returns, orders, and compliance.

faqs.question: What taxes are covered?
faqs.answer: Income tax, GST, and other applicable direct/indirect taxes.

faqs.question: Are contingent liabilities disclosed in the prospectus?
faqs.answer: Yes, material contingent tax liabilities require disclosure.

faqs.question: Who uses this report?
faqs.answer: Merchant bankers, auditors, and the board for prospectus preparation.

IPO Financial Due Diligence.shortDescription: Comprehensive financial due diligence assessment of company financials before IPO filing.
IPO Financial Due Diligence.longDescription: We conduct detailed financial due diligence covering revenue recognition, working capital, and quality of earnings to support accurate prospectus disclosures.
features: Working capital and cash flow analysis

process.title: Scope Definition
process.description: Define financial diligence scope and periods.

process.title: Detailed Review
process.description: Analyze financials, policies, and quality of earnings.

faqs.question: What is quality of earnings analysis?
faqs.answer: An assessment of how sustainable and accurate reported earnings actually are.

faqs.question: Who conducts this diligence?
faqs.answer: Independent financial advisors, often alongside statutory auditors.

faqs.question: How does this differ from statutory audit?
faqs.answer: It's a deeper, transaction-focused analysis beyond standard audit procedures.

IPO Tax Structuring.shortDescription: Advisory on tax-efficient structuring of the IPO transaction and pre-IPO arrangements.
IPO Tax Structuring.longDescription: We advise on tax-efficient structuring for pre-IPO restructuring, offer-for-sale arrangements, and ESOP taxation to optimize outcomes for the company and stakeholders.
benefits: Optimized outcomes for promoters and investors

process.title: Tax Analysis
process.description: Assess tax implications and optimization options.

faqs.question: What is an offer for sale?
faqs.answer: A component of IPO where existing shareholders sell shares to the public.

faqs.question: How is ESOP taxed at IPO?
faqs.answer: Perquisite tax at exercise and capital gains tax at sale, subject to conditions.

faqs.question: Does tax structuring affect issue timeline?
faqs.answer: It should be planned well in advance to avoid delays.

IPO ESOP Compliance.shortDescription: Ensure ESOP scheme compliance with SEBI regulations ahead of and after the IPO.
IPO ESOP Compliance.longDescription: We review and align your ESOP scheme with SEBI SBEB regulations applicable to listed companies, covering vesting, exercise, and disclosure requirements.
benefits: Compliant ESOP scheme for listed status

process.title: Scheme Review
process.description: Assess current ESOP scheme against SEBI norms.

faqs.question: Do pre-IPO ESOP schemes need modification?
faqs.answer: Often yes, to align with SEBI SBEB regulations for listed entities.

faqs.question: Is shareholder approval required for ESOP schemes?
faqs.answer: Yes, listed company ESOP schemes require shareholder approval.

faqs.question: Are ESOP grants disclosed in the prospectus?
faqs.answer: Yes, material ESOP details are disclosed.

IPO Share Capital Compliance.shortDescription: Ensure share capital structure and issuance history comply with IPO eligibility requirements.
IPO Share Capital Compliance.longDescription: We review the history of share issuances, bonus shares, and capital changes to confirm compliance with SEBI's IPO eligibility norms.

faqs.question: What is the minimum promoter holding period?
faqs.answer: Shares held for at least one year before filing are generally counted toward eligibility.

faqs.question: Are bonus shares treated differently?
faqs.answer: They generally take the holding period of the original shares.

faqs.question: What if past issuances weren't properly documented?
faqs.answer: Remedial documentation may be needed before proceeding.

IPO Corporate Secretarial Support.shortDescription: Manage corporate secretarial requirements including board approvals throughout the IPO process.
IPO Corporate Secretarial Support.longDescription: We handle board and shareholder resolutions, statutory filings, and secretarial documentation required at each stage of the IPO process.
benefits: Timely approvals at each IPO stage

process.title: Milestone Mapping
process.description: Identify secretarial requirements per IPO stage.

process.title: Documentation
process.description: Prepare resolutions and filings as needed.

process.title: Compliance Confirmation
process.description: Confirm timely completion of each requirement.

faqs.question: What approvals are needed during an IPO?
faqs.answer: Board and shareholder approvals for the issue, ESOP schemes, and related matters.

faqs.question: Is a company secretary mandatory during IPO?
faqs.answer: Yes, professional secretarial support is essential for compliance.

faqs.question: Does this continue post-listing?
faqs.answer: Yes, secretarial compliance continues as an ongoing listed-company obligation.

IPO Board & Shareholder Approvals.shortDescription: Manage the board and shareholder approval process required for various IPO-related resolutions.
IPO Board & Shareholder Approvals.longDescription: We coordinate the drafting, notice, and passing of board and shareholder resolutions required to authorize the IPO and related corporate actions.
benefits: Legally valid authorization for the IPO

faqs.question: What resolutions are needed for an IPO?
faqs.answer: Approval of the issue, offer document, and related authorizations.

faqs.question: Is special resolution required?
faqs.answer: Yes, for certain matters like fresh issue of capital.

faqs.question: Can approvals be obtained by postal ballot?
faqs.answer: Yes, where physical meetings aren't feasible for all shareholders.

IPO Legal Documentation.shortDescription: Prepare and coordinate legal documentation required throughout the IPO process.
IPO Legal Documentation.longDescription: We manage the preparation of underwriting agreements, escrow agreements, and other legal documents essential to executing the IPO.

faqs.question: What is an underwriting agreement?
faqs.answer: An agreement where underwriters commit to subscribe to unsubscribed shares.

faqs.question: Why is an escrow account needed?
faqs.answer: To hold investor application money securely until allotment.

faqs.question: How many parties are typically involved?
faqs.answer: The company, merchant bankers, registrars, and bankers to the issue.

IPO Regulatory Representation.shortDescription: Represent your company before SEBI and other regulators during the IPO approval process.
IPO Regulatory Representation.longDescription: We represent the company in interactions with SEBI, exchanges, and other regulators, addressing queries and observations throughout the IPO process.
benefits: Faster resolution of queries and observations

faqs.question: What are SEBI observations?
faqs.answer: Comments or queries raised by SEBI on the draft offer document requiring response.

faqs.question: How long does SEBI take to respond?
faqs.answer: Typically within a specified statutory period after DRHP filing.

faqs.question: Can the IPO proceed without addressing observations?
faqs.answer: No, all material observations must be addressed before further progress.

Post-IPO Legal Compliance.shortDescription: Manage ongoing legal compliance obligations for your company after successful listing.
Post-IPO Legal Compliance.longDescription: We help establish and manage post-listing legal compliance covering periodic disclosures, governance requirements, and regulatory filings.
benefits: Peace of mind for newly listed companies

faqs.question: What is LODR?
faqs.answer: SEBI's Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements regulations for listed entities.

faqs.question: What are common post-listing filings?
faqs.answer: Quarterly results, shareholding pattern, and corporate governance reports.

faqs.question: What happens on non-compliance?
faqs.answer: Penalties, freezing of promoter shares, or other regulatory action may apply.

Share Transfer Services.shortDescription: Process physical and demat share transfers for shareholders efficiently and compliantly.
Share Transfer Services.longDescription: We manage share transfer requests, verify documentation, and coordinate with the RTA to ensure smooth transfer of ownership for shareholders.

process.title: Processing
process.description: Submit to RTA for transfer processing.

faqs.question: Can physical shares still be transferred?
faqs.answer: Physical transfers are largely restricted; dematerialization is generally required first.

faqs.question: What is an RTA?
faqs.answer: Registrar and Transfer Agent, managing shareholder records for listed companies.

faqs.question: How long does demat transfer take?
faqs.answer: Typically completed within a few working days via depository participants.

Share Transmission Services.shortDescription: Manage share transmission processes following the death or incapacity of a shareholder.
Share Transmission Services.longDescription: We assist legal heirs with transmission of shares, verifying succession documents and coordinating with the RTA for smooth processing.
benefits: Smooth transfer of shares to legal heirs
Clear guidance through the transmission process

process.title: Confirmation
process.description: Receive updated holding in heir's name.

faqs.question: What documents are needed for transmission?
faqs.answer: Death certificate, succession proof, and identity documents of the claimant.

faqs.question: Is nomination helpful for transmission?
faqs.answer: Yes, a valid nomination significantly simplifies the process.

faqs.question: What if there's no will or nomination?
faqs.answer: A succession certificate from the court is typically required.

Duplicate Share Certificate.shortDescription: Assist shareholders in obtaining duplicate share certificates for lost or damaged originals.
Duplicate Share Certificate.longDescription: We help shareholders navigate the process of obtaining duplicate certificates, including affidavits, indemnity, and RTA coordination.

faqs.question: Is a public notice always required?
faqs.answer: Often required for high-value holdings as a fraud-prevention measure.

faqs.question: Can I dematerialize instead of getting a duplicate?
faqs.answer: Yes, converting to demat form is often the more efficient long-term option.

faqs.question: Is a police complaint needed?
faqs.answer: Recommended in cases of theft, though not always mandatory for loss.

Dematerialization of Shares.shortDescription: Convert your physical share certificates into electronic demat form.
Dematerialization of Shares.longDescription: We assist in converting physical shares to demat form through your depository participant, ensuring accurate processing and updated holdings.
benefits: Safer, more liquid holding of shares
Eliminates risk of physical certificate loss

process.title: Submission
process.description: Submit certificates and DRF via the DP.

faqs.question: Is dematerialization mandatory?
faqs.answer: For trading on exchanges, yes; physical shares can no longer be traded.

faqs.question: What if certificate name differs from PAN records?
faqs.answer: Name correction/linking documentation may be required.

faqs.question: How long does the process take?
faqs.answer: Typically 2-3 weeks depending on RTA processing.

Rematerialization of Shares.shortDescription: Convert electronic demat shares back into physical certificate form when needed.
Rematerialization of Shares.longDescription: In specific cases, shareholders may need physical certificates again. We manage the rematerialization request process through your depository participant.
benefits: Professional handling of the request process

faqs.question: Why would someone rematerialize shares?
faqs.answer: Specific legal, inheritance, or personal preference reasons.

faqs.question: Can rematerialized shares be traded on exchanges?
faqs.answer: No, they must be dematerialized again before trading.

faqs.question: Is there a fee for rematerialization?
faqs.answer: Yes, nominal fees apply as per depository participant charges.

Address Change Services.shortDescription: Update your registered address with the company's records through the RTA.
Address Change Services.longDescription: We help shareholders update their address in company records, ensuring timely delivery of dividends, notices, and statements.

process.title: Document Collection
process.description: Gather address proof and account details.

faqs.question: Is this different for physical and demat holdings?
faqs.answer: Physical holdings update via RTA directly; demat updates via your DP.

faqs.question: What proof is accepted for address change?
faqs.answer: Aadhaar, passport, utility bill, or other standard address proofs.

faqs.question: How long until the update reflects?
faqs.answer: Typically within a week of submission.

Bank Details Updation.shortDescription: Update your bank account details for accurate dividend and refund credits.
Bank Details Updation.longDescription: We assist shareholders in updating bank account details with the RTA/DP to ensure dividends and refunds are credited correctly.
benefits: Reduces risk of failed payment credits

process.title: Document Collection
process.description: Gather bank proof and account details.

process.title: Confirmation
process.description: Confirm updated bank details in records.

faqs.question: Why is bank detail updation important?
faqs.answer: To avoid failed or delayed dividend and refund payments.

faqs.question: Can demat account bank details be updated online?
faqs.answer: Yes, many DPs offer online mandate update facilities.

faqs.question: What if payment fails due to outdated details?
faqs.answer: It will be reprocessed or held until details are corrected.

Email & Mobile Updation.shortDescription: Update your registered email and mobile number for timely shareholder communications.
Email & Mobile Updation.longDescription: We help shareholders update contact details in company records to ensure timely receipt of notices, e-voting information, and alerts.
benefits: Ensures timely e-voting and notice receipt

faqs.question: Is email registration mandatory now?
faqs.answer: SEBI encourages it strongly for e-voting and paperless communication.

faqs.question: Can this be done online?
faqs.answer: Yes, many RTAs and DPs offer online self-service updates.

faqs.question: What if I miss e-voting due to outdated contact?
faqs.answer: Update your details promptly to avoid missing future corporate actions.

PAN Updation.shortDescription: Update or link your PAN details with your shareholding records for compliance.
PAN Updation.longDescription: We assist shareholders in updating or correcting PAN details in their folio/demat records to comply with regulatory linkage requirements.

faqs.question: Is PAN mandatory for holding shares?
faqs.answer: Yes, for both physical and demat holdings currently.

faqs.question: What happens if PAN isn't updated?
faqs.answer: Folios may be frozen for debit transactions until KYC is completed.

faqs.question: Can joint holders have different PANs updated?
faqs.answer: Yes, PAN of all joint holders must be updated.

KYC Updation.shortDescription: Complete or update your KYC details as mandated for shareholder folios and demat accounts.
KYC Updation.longDescription: We help shareholders complete mandatory KYC requirements — PAN, address, bank, and nomination — to keep folios active and compliant.

process.title: Confirmation
process.description: Confirm KYC completion and active folio status.

faqs.question: Why is KYC mandatory for shareholders?
faqs.answer: SEBI mandates complete KYC to prevent unauthorized transactions and fraud.

faqs.question: What happens if KYC is incomplete?
faqs.answer: The folio may be frozen for debit transactions like transfer or transmission.

faqs.question: Is nomination part of mandatory KYC?
faqs.answer: Yes, nomination is now a mandatory field for most holdings.

Nomination Services.shortDescription: Register or update nomination details for your shareholding to simplify future transmission.
Nomination Services.longDescription: We help shareholders complete nomination forms, ensuring smooth future transmission of shares to nominated beneficiaries without disputes.

faqs.question: Is nomination mandatory now?
faqs.answer: Yes, SEBI has made nomination mandatory or requires explicit opt-out.

faqs.question: Can nomination be changed later?
faqs.answer: Yes, a new nomination form supersedes the earlier one.

faqs.question: Does nomination override a will?
faqs.answer: This is a nuanced legal area; consulting on specific circumstances is advisable.

Dividend Processing.shortDescription: Assist with tracking, claiming, and resolving dividend payment issues for shareholders.
Dividend Processing.longDescription: We help shareholders track dividend payments, resolve credit failures, and ensure timely receipt of declared dividends.

process.title: Issue Resolution
process.description: Address credit failures with the RTA.

faqs.question: Why do dividend payments sometimes fail?
faqs.answer: Outdated bank details or unvalidated bank accounts, among other reasons.

faqs.question: How is dividend paid for demat holdings?
faqs.answer: Directly credited to the bank account linked to the demat account.

faqs.question: What if the dividend was never received?
faqs.answer: It can be reissued after verification with the RTA.

Unpaid Dividend Services.shortDescription: Claim unpaid or unclaimed dividends transferred to the Unpaid Dividend Account.
Unpaid Dividend Services.longDescription: We help shareholders claim dividends that remain unpaid due to processing issues, coordinating with the company and RTA for release.

process.title: Release
process.description: Follow up until payment is released.

faqs.question: What is an Unpaid Dividend Account?
faqs.answer: A separate account where undelivered dividend amounts are held for 7 years.

faqs.question: What happens after 7 years?
faqs.answer: Unclaimed amounts are transferred to the Investor Education and Protection Fund.

faqs.question: Can dividends be claimed from IEPF too?
faqs.answer: Yes, through a separate IEPF claim process.

Dividend Revalidation.shortDescription: Revalidate expired dividend warrants or cheques to receive your due payment.
Dividend Revalidation.longDescription: We help shareholders revalidate expired dividend instruments, coordinating with the company/RTA to reissue or credit the amount.

process.title: Verification
process.description: Confirm expiry and eligibility for revalidation.

faqs.question: How long is a dividend warrant valid?
faqs.answer: Typically 3 months from the date of issue.

faqs.question: Can an expired warrant always be revalidated?
faqs.answer: Generally yes, within the 7-year unpaid dividend window.

faqs.question: Is direct bank credit preferable?
faqs.answer: Yes, it avoids the need for physical instrument revalidation altogether.

Investor Grievance Handling.shortDescription: Assist shareholders in resolving grievances related to shares, dividends, or company communication.
Investor Grievance Handling.longDescription: We help investors draft and file grievances with the company, RTA, or SEBI's SCORES platform, ensuring proper follow-up until resolution.
benefits: Access to SEBI's investor grievance mechanism

process.title: Grievance Documentation
process.description: Compile details and evidence of the issue.

process.title: Filing
process.description: Submit grievance to company/RTA or SCORES.

faqs.question: What is SEBI SCORES?
faqs.answer: SEBI's online platform for filing and tracking investor complaints.

faqs.question: What issues can be raised as grievances?
faqs.answer: Non-receipt of dividends, transfer delays, or communication failures, among others.

faqs.question: How long does resolution typically take?
faqs.answer: Companies are required to respond within a specified regulatory timeline.

Shareholder Reconciliation.shortDescription: Reconcile shareholder records between the company, RTA, and depositories for accuracy.
Shareholder Reconciliation.longDescription: We perform reconciliation of shareholder records across physical and demat holdings, identifying and resolving discrepancies for accurate records.

process.title: Data Compilation
process.description: Gather records from RTA and depositories.

faqs.question: Why do shareholder records need reconciliation?
faqs.answer: To ensure company records match depository data exactly for compliance and accuracy.

faqs.question: How often is this done?
faqs.answer: Regularly, and especially before corporate actions like dividends or splits.

faqs.question: What causes discrepancies?
faqs.answer: Processing delays, data entry errors, or unresolved corporate action records.

Corporate Action Processing.shortDescription: Process corporate actions like dividends, bonuses, and splits across shareholder records.
Corporate Action Processing.longDescription: We manage the end-to-end processing of corporate actions, ensuring accurate implementation across RTA and depository records.
requirements: Corporate action details (type, ratio, record date)

process.title: Action Planning
process.description: Define corporate action parameters and timeline.

faqs.question: What are common corporate actions?
faqs.answer: Dividends, bonus issues, stock splits, and rights issues.

faqs.question: What is a record date?
faqs.answer: The date determining shareholder eligibility for a corporate action.

faqs.question: Who processes corporate actions?
faqs.answer: The company's RTA, coordinating with depositories and exchanges.

Bonus Issue Processing.shortDescription: Manage the complete process of issuing and crediting bonus shares to eligible shareholders.
Bonus Issue Processing.longDescription: We coordinate bonus share issuance from board approval through to crediting shares in eligible shareholders' demat accounts.
features: Bonus ratio and record date coordination

process.title: Processing
process.description: Coordinate bonus share credit with RTA/NSDL/CDSL.

faqs.question: What is a bonus issue?
faqs.answer: Free additional shares issued to existing shareholders from reserves.

faqs.question: Is shareholder approval required?
faqs.answer: Yes, an ordinary resolution is generally required.

faqs.question: How long until bonus shares are credited?
faqs.answer: Typically within 15 days of the record date.

Rights Issue Processing.shortDescription: Manage the rights issue process from entitlement calculation to share allotment.
Rights Issue Processing.longDescription: We coordinate rights issue processing including entitlement ratio application, subscription tracking, and allotment for eligible shareholders.

process.title: Allotment
process.description: Process final allotment and credit shares.

faqs.question: What is a rights issue?
faqs.answer: An offer to existing shareholders to buy additional shares, usually at a discount.

faqs.question: Can rights entitlements be traded?
faqs.answer: Yes, rights entitlements can be renounced or traded during the issue period.

faqs.question: What if a shareholder doesn't subscribe?
faqs.answer: Unsubscribed shares may be allotted to other applicants as per the offer terms.

Stock Split Processing.shortDescription: Manage the stock split process ensuring accurate share credit at the revised face value.
Stock Split Processing.longDescription: We coordinate stock split implementation, ensuring shareholder holdings are accurately adjusted to the new face value and quantity.
features: Split ratio and record date coordination
requirements: Current face value and split ratio

faqs.question: What is a stock split?
faqs.answer: Dividing existing shares into multiple shares of lower face value, increasing share count.

faqs.question: Does a stock split change investment value?
faqs.answer: No, total investment value remains the same, only the number of shares changes.

faqs.question: Is shareholder approval needed for a split?
faqs.answer: Yes, typically via ordinary resolution.

Merger & Amalgamation Processing.shortDescription: Process shareholding changes resulting from a merger or amalgamation scheme.
Merger & Amalgamation Processing.longDescription: We manage the RTA-side implementation of merger schemes, including share swap ratio application and crediting shares of the resulting entity.
features: Swap ratio application to shareholder records

process.title: Scheme Review
process.description: Understand the sanctioned scheme and swap ratio.

process.title: Processing
process.description: Coordinate share credit as per swap ratio.

faqs.question: What is a swap ratio?
faqs.answer: The ratio at which shares of the merging company are exchanged for shares of the resulting company.

faqs.question: Is NCLT approval required before implementation?
faqs.answer: Yes, the scheme must be sanctioned before RTA processing begins.

faqs.question: What happens to fractional shares?
faqs.answer: They are typically consolidated and sold, with proceeds distributed to shareholders.

IPO RTA Services.shortDescription: Comprehensive Registrar and Transfer Agent services supporting the IPO application and allotment process.
IPO RTA Services.longDescription: We provide end-to-end RTA coordination for IPOs, covering application processing, allotment, and post-issue shareholder services.

process.title: Post-Issue Services
process.description: Set up ongoing shareholder record services.

faqs.question: What does an RTA do during an IPO?
faqs.answer: Processes applications, determines allotment, and manages refunds and share credits.

faqs.question: Is RTA appointment mandatory for IPOs?
faqs.answer: Yes, SEBI mandates a registered RTA for the issue process.

faqs.question: Does RTA service continue post-listing?
faqs.answer: Yes, for ongoing shareholder record management.

IPO Application Processing.shortDescription: Process IPO applications from investors ensuring accurate data capture and validation.
IPO Application Processing.longDescription: We manage the processing of investor applications received through ASBA and UPI mechanisms, ensuring data accuracy for allotment.

process.title: Data Collection
process.description: Gather application data from all channels.

process.title: Validation
process.description: Screen for duplicates and technical rejections.

faqs.question: What is a technical rejection?
faqs.answer: An application rejected for procedural reasons like incomplete details or mismatched signatures.

faqs.question: What is ASBA?
faqs.answer: Application Supported by Blocked Amount, a mechanism blocking funds until allotment.

faqs.question: How are duplicate applications handled?
faqs.answer: Identified and consolidated or rejected as per SEBI norms.

IPO Allotment Services.shortDescription: Manage the share allotment process ensuring fair, compliant distribution to applicants.
IPO Allotment Services.longDescription: We coordinate the allotment process following SEBI's basis of allotment guidelines, ensuring fair distribution across investor categories.

process.title: Allotment Computation
process.description: Compute allotment as per SEBI basis.

process.title: Approval & Finalization
process.description: Obtain exchange approval and finalize allotment.

faqs.question: What is 'basis of allotment'?
faqs.answer: The methodology, approved by exchanges, for distributing shares among applicants.

faqs.question: How are oversubscribed categories handled?
faqs.answer: Through proportionate allotment or lottery, as per SEBI rules.

faqs.question: When is allotment typically finalized?
faqs.answer: Within a few days of the issue closing, per the IPO timeline.

Refund Processing.shortDescription: Manage refund processing for unsuccessful or partially allotted IPO applicants.
Refund Processing.longDescription: We coordinate the release of blocked funds for unsuccessful or partially allotted applications, ensuring timely refund processing.

faqs.question: How quickly must refunds be processed?
faqs.answer: SEBI mandates refunds/unblocking within a specified short timeline post-allotment.

faqs.question: What happens to ASBA amounts for successful applicants?
faqs.answer: The blocked amount is debited corresponding to the shares allotted.

faqs.question: What if a refund fails?
faqs.answer: It is investigated and reprocessed with corrected details.

NCD & Bond Services.shortDescription: Manage registrar services for Non-Convertible Debenture and bond issuances.
NCD & Bond Services.longDescription: We provide RTA services for NCD and bond issues, covering application processing, allotment, and ongoing investor servicing.

process.title: Application Processing
process.description: Process investor applications for the issue.

process.title: Allotment
process.description: Finalize allotment as per issue terms.

faqs.question: What is an NCD?
faqs.answer: Non-Convertible Debenture, a debt instrument that cannot be converted into equity.

faqs.question: How is interest paid on NCDs?
faqs.answer: As per the frequency specified in the offer document — monthly, annual, or cumulative.

faqs.question: Is RTA involved throughout the NCD tenure?
faqs.answer: Yes, for interest payments, redemption, and investor record maintenance.

Debenture Redemption Services.shortDescription: Manage the redemption process for debentures at maturity ensuring timely payment to holders.
Debenture Redemption Services.longDescription: We coordinate debenture redemption at maturity, verifying holder records and ensuring timely principal repayment through the RTA.

faqs.question: What is debenture redemption?
faqs.answer: Repayment of the principal amount to debenture holders at maturity.

faqs.question: Is a debenture redemption reserve required?
faqs.answer: Yes, companies typically maintain a reserve as per applicable rules.

faqs.question: What if a holder's details are outdated?
faqs.answer: Payment may be delayed until records are updated or unclaimed processes apply.

Interest Payment Services.shortDescription: Manage periodic interest payment processing for bondholders and debenture holders.
Interest Payment Services.longDescription: We coordinate periodic interest payments to bond and debenture holders, ensuring accurate computation and timely disbursement.

process.title: TDS Processing
process.description: Deduct and account for applicable TDS.

faqs.question: Is TDS applicable on interest payments?
faqs.answer: Yes, subject to prescribed thresholds and holder-specific exemptions.

faqs.question: How often are interest payments made?
faqs.answer: As per the schedule specified in the offer document — monthly, quarterly, or annually.

faqs.question: What if a holder's bank details fail?
faqs.answer: Payment is held and reprocessed after correcting the details.

Redemption Processing.shortDescription: Manage principal redemption processing across various financial instruments at maturity.
Redemption Processing.longDescription: We handle end-to-end redemption processing for maturing financial instruments, coordinating accurate computation and disbursement to holders.

faqs.question: What instruments require redemption processing?
faqs.answer: Debentures, bonds, and other maturing financial instruments.

faqs.question: Is early redemption possible?
faqs.answer: Only if the instrument terms specifically permit a call/put option.

faqs.question: What if redemption isn't claimed?
faqs.answer: Amounts follow unclaimed fund rules similar to unpaid dividends.

Unclaimed Securities Services.shortDescription: Help investors identify and claim unclaimed securities lying with the company or IEPF.
Unclaimed Securities Services.longDescription: We help investors trace unclaimed shares, dividends, or other securities and navigate the claim process with the company or IEPF authority.
requirements: Identity proof of the claimant/legal heir

process.title: Tracing
process.description: Identify unclaimed securities and their status.

process.title: Application Filing
process.description: Prepare and file the claim application.

process.title: Resolution
process.description: Follow up until securities/proceeds are released.

faqs.question: How do securities become unclaimed?
faqs.answer: Due to outdated contact details, unclaimed dividends, or unprocessed transmissions.

faqs.question: Where do very old unclaimed shares go?
faqs.answer: They are transferred to the Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF).

faqs.question: Can legal heirs claim unclaimed shares?
faqs.answer: Yes, with appropriate succession documentation.

IEPF Claim Assistance.shortDescription: Assist investors in claiming shares and dividends transferred to the IEPF.
IEPF Claim Assistance.longDescription: We manage the complete IEPF claim process, including Form IEPF-5 filing, entitlement letter, and coordination with the company and IEPF authority.
benefits: Professional handling of complex claim process

process.title: Eligibility Verification
process.description: Confirm details of the transferred securities.

process.title: Verification & Claim
process.description: Coordinate company verification and claim release.

faqs.question: What is IEPF-5?
faqs.answer: The application form for claiming shares/dividends transferred to the IEPF.

faqs.question: How long does an IEPF claim take?
faqs.answer: Typically 60-90 days, given verification requirements at multiple stages.

faqs.question: Is company verification mandatory?
faqs.answer: Yes, the company must verify and confirm the claim before IEPF releases it.

IEPF Transfer Compliance.shortDescription: Ensure company compliance in transferring unclaimed shares and dividends to the IEPF as required.
IEPF Transfer Compliance.longDescription: We help companies comply with IEPF transfer obligations, including notice requirements, record maintenance, and timely transfer of unclaimed amounts.

faqs.question: When must shares be transferred to IEPF?
faqs.answer: When dividends remain unpaid for 7 consecutive years.

faqs.question: Is shareholder notice mandatory before transfer?
faqs.answer: Yes, individual and public notice is required before transfer.

faqs.question: Can transferred shares be reclaimed by the original holder?
faqs.answer: Yes, through the IEPF-5 claim process.

Register of Members Maintenance.shortDescription: Maintain accurate and updated Register of Members as required under the Companies Act.
Register of Members Maintenance.longDescription: We help listed and unlisted companies maintain a compliant, accurate Register of Members reflecting all shareholding changes.

process.title: Update & Reconciliation
process.description: Update register and reconcile with sources.

process.title: Ongoing Maintenance
process.description: Maintain the register as transactions occur.

faqs.question: Is Register of Members mandatory?
faqs.answer: Yes, under Section 88 of the Companies Act.

faqs.question: Who maintains it for listed companies?
faqs.answer: Typically the RTA on behalf of the company.

faqs.question: Can members inspect the register?
faqs.answer: Yes, subject to reasonable conditions specified by the company.

Beneficial Owner Reconciliation.shortDescription: Reconcile beneficial ownership records between depositories and company registers.
Beneficial Owner Reconciliation.longDescription: We perform periodic reconciliation of beneficial owner data across NSDL, CDSL, and company records to ensure accuracy and regulatory compliance.
benefits: Reduces risk of regulatory discrepancy findings

faqs.question: How often is this reconciliation required?
faqs.answer: Typically monthly for listed companies, as per SEBI/depository requirements.

faqs.question: Who certifies this reconciliation?
faqs.answer: Often a practicing company secretary as part of secretarial compliance.

faqs.question: What causes discrepancies?
faqs.answer: Processing delays, in-transit corporate actions, or unprocessed transfers.

Demat Reconciliation.shortDescription: Reconcile demat account holdings with company records for accuracy and compliance.
Demat Reconciliation.longDescription: We reconcile demat holdings across depository participants against the company's total issued capital to ensure consistent, accurate records.
requirements: Total issued and paid-up capital details

process.title: Data Compilation
process.description: Gather demat and issued capital data.

process.title: Reporting
process.description: Prepare reconciliation report and resolution plan.

faqs.question: Why reconcile demat holdings?
faqs.answer: To ensure total demat and physical holdings match the company's issued capital.

faqs.question: Is this a regulatory requirement?
faqs.answer: Yes, periodic reconciliation is mandated for listed companies.

faqs.question: What if a mismatch is found?
faqs.answer: It must be investigated and resolved promptly with the RTA and depositories.

Corporate Action Reconciliation.shortDescription: Reconcile corporate action outcomes such as dividends and bonuses against shareholder records.
Corporate Action Reconciliation.longDescription: We verify that corporate actions like dividends, bonuses, and splits have been accurately reflected across all shareholder records.

process.title: Data Collection
process.description: Gather corporate action and record data.

faqs.question: When should this reconciliation be done?
faqs.answer: Shortly after each corporate action is implemented.

faqs.question: What errors are commonly found?
faqs.answer: Missed shareholders, incorrect ratios, or delayed processing.

faqs.question: Does this affect regulatory compliance?
faqs.answer: Yes, accurate implementation is part of listing compliance obligations.

Annual Return Data Support.shortDescription: Provide shareholder and compliance data support for the company's annual return filing.
Annual Return Data Support.longDescription: We compile shareholding pattern, transfer history, and other RTA-held data required for accurate MGT-7 annual return preparation.
benefits: Reduced coordination burden for compliance teams
Timely data availability for filing deadlines

process.title: Delivery
process.description: Provide data to the company secretarial team.

faqs.question: What data does the RTA typically provide?
faqs.answer: Shareholding pattern, transfer history, and beneficial ownership details.

faqs.question: Is this coordinated with the company secretary?
faqs.answer: Yes, to ensure the annual return is prepared accurately and on time.

faqs.question: How far in advance should this be requested?
faqs.answer: At least a few weeks before the MGT-7 filing deadline.

Investor Communication Services.shortDescription: Manage shareholder communication including notices, annual reports, and corporate updates.
Investor Communication Services.longDescription: We help companies manage timely and compliant communication with shareholders, covering notices, annual reports, and e-voting information.
benefits: Reduced risk of missed disclosure timelines

process.title: Database Preparation
process.description: Verify and prepare shareholder contact data.

faqs.question: Is electronic communication sufficient?
faqs.answer: Yes, for shareholders with registered email, subject to regulatory conditions.

faqs.question: What must be communicated before AGM?
faqs.answer: Notice, annual report, and e-voting instructions within prescribed timelines.

faqs.question: What if a shareholder hasn't registered email?
faqs.answer: Physical communication may be required as per applicable rules.

Shareholder Statement Services.shortDescription: Generate and distribute shareholding statements and holding certificates for investors.
Shareholder Statement Services.longDescription: We help shareholders and companies generate accurate holding statements, transaction summaries, and certificates as needed for various purposes.
benefits: Accurate proof of shareholding for various uses
Useful for loans, KYC, or legal purposes

process.title: Delivery
process.description: Deliver the statement to the shareholder.

faqs.question: What is a shareholding statement used for?
faqs.answer: Loan applications, legal proceedings, or personal record-keeping.

faqs.question: Can statements cover historical transactions?
faqs.answer: Yes, transaction history over a specified period can be provided.

faqs.question: Is there a fee for such statements?
faqs.answer: Nominal charges may apply depending on the RTA/DP.

RTA Compliance Support.shortDescription: Support companies in meeting RTA-related regulatory compliance requirements under SEBI norms.
RTA Compliance Support.longDescription: We help companies ensure their RTA arrangements and related processes comply with SEBI's regulatory framework for registrar services.

faqs.question: What SEBI regulations govern RTAs?
faqs.answer: SEBI (Registrars to an Issue and Share Transfer Agents) Regulations.

faqs.question: Is RTA appointment mandatory for listed companies?
faqs.answer: Yes, listed companies must engage a SEBI-registered RTA.

faqs.question: What compliance issues are common?
faqs.answer: Delayed reconciliation, grievance redressal delays, and reporting gaps.
